description.p: FerDim is a download manager for Linux with a segmented, multi-connection engine that tunes itself to the line or the server, whichever ceiling is reachable first.

ul.li: Up to 32 parallel connections per job with work stealing and crash-safe resume
A throughput governor that adapts to HTTP 429/503 limits and stalled servers
Speed limits, a night scheduler and a smart queue
FTP/FTPS, HLS and DASH downloads, checksum and Merkle verification
Archive browsing and extraction, metalink support, watched folders
A GTK 4 app, a CLI, a local web UI and a Firefox extension

description.p: Available in English, Turkish, Spanish and Russian.

screenshot.caption: The GTK 4 window with live per-job speeds and controls
The dependency-free web UI served by the daemon

description.p: Build fix for fast builders; no functional changes.
Data integrity and crash safety: safer resume, power-cut durability, corrupt queue recovery and soft-404 warnings.
Build fix for slow builders; no functional changes.
Security fixes: the web page no longer carries the API token, HTTP download folders are confined and credentials stay on their origin.

Manifest V3 browser extension, time-of-day speed plan, a local metrics endpoint, congestion-aware link scaling, HTTP/3 connection reuse, an opt-in LAN peer cache and hardening of the local web server.
Learned per-host connection profiles, archive browsing and extraction, desktop notifications, a D-Bus bridge and a GNOME Shell extension.
